method.label: Subtract a sector from a kite

annotationRationale: Sector area, tangent perpendicularity, and area decomposition drive the solution. The tangent angle-bisector theorem and the 30-degree right-triangle property supply needed angles and lengths. cnm_263 remains supporting background, with no US curriculum alignment asserted.
sourceMethod: Followed the official radius-one, kite-minus-sector method. Clarified the center's position beyond BC and why subtracting the sector gives exactly the desired region.

review.mathCheck: With radius 1, AO=2 and BC=√3. The kite has area √3, and its 120° sector has area π/3. Their difference divided by triangle area 3√3/4 gives \(4/3-4\sqrt3\pi/27\), choice E. The center location and region subtraction are correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful expansion of MAA #22's radius normalization and kite-minus-sector approach. The added decomposition explains why the subtraction gives precisely the required region.
review.annotationCheck: The statement, E key and method annotation agree. The explanation reconstructs the configuration without needing a question figure.
